req.title: AWS Solutions Architect, 2027 full time, L4, AWSI Emerging Talent Program
req.source: Recruiter confirmation on October 21, 2026, and the recruiter's study guide, supplied by the candidate. Contact details are not stored here.

event.note: Confirmed by the recruiter on October 21. Four 60-minute interviews with four interviewers, with a lunch break from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm. Arrive by 9:00 am.

role.summary: Customer-facing, pre-sales architecture. You help customers understand what to build on AWS and why. This is not a software engineering loop.
focus: Understand a customer problem, then recommend and explain an AWS design against their requirements.
Work with sales and adapt the depth of an explanation from engineers to executives.
Judge success by customer impact, not by the cleverness of the design.

streams.title: Technical evaluation
streams.summary: No live coding and no data structures round. Instead, a thorough discussion of coding concepts and principles: you explain code and ideas out loud.

parts.label: Breadth
parts.text: Three areas from: CS fundamentals, databases and analytics, networking, hardware, application development, security, AI/ML. Cloud computing is also on the prep list.

parts.label: Depth
parts.text: One area, explored until you reach the edge of what you know.

parts.label: Explain it simply
parts.text: Explain a technical idea to a non-technical audience. The recruiter repeated this four times: treat it as the most important skill of the day.

streams.title: Leadership Principles
streams.summary: Expect LP questions in every round. Eight principles were named as most relevant to this role.

parts.label: Named LPs
parts.text: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Bias for Action, Earn Trust, Learn and Be Curious, Insist on the Highest Standards, Deliver Results, Dive Deep.

parts.label: Answer length
parts.text: 2 to 4 minutes per story, STAR, with a metric in every result.

parts.label: Follow-ups
parts.text: Be ready for "How would you implement this at AWS?" and "What would you do differently?"

streams.title: Communication assessment
streams.summary: An 8 to 10 minute oral presentation on a topic you choose, then brief Q&A. No laptop and no slides. Simple handouts, diagrams, or props are allowed.

parts.label: Audience
parts.text: Technical professionals who do not know your topic.

parts.label: Scored on
parts.text: Clarity, engagement, organization, confidence and presence, time management, and a clear call to action.

parts.label: Your topic
parts.text: How do you fit a big AI model on a small computer? Quantization explained, built on ModelScope.

focus_areas.note: Interviewers choose the questions, so the backup areas get a lighter pass too.

answer_rubric: Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
Speak for 2 to 4 minutes, not 60 to 90 seconds.
Put a metric in every result.
Use examples from the last 5 years.
Each answer should show 4 to 6 Leadership Principles.
Be ready for "How would you implement this at AWS?" and "What would you do differently?"

checklist.text: Write the interviewer's name at the top of a fresh notebook page.
After the round, note which stories you told and which LPs they asked about.
Ask one question of your own in the last 5 minutes.
Write the interviewer's name at the top of a fresh page.
Check your log: lead with stories you have not told yet.
Ask one question of your own.
At lunch: water, a short walk, reread the day-of sheet once. Do not cram.
Lead with stories you have not told yet.
Ask one question of your own.
Last round: same energy as the first. Smile, slow down.
Use any remaining lead stories; reuse a story only from a new angle.
Ask one question of your own and thank the interviewer.

round_expect: Leadership Principle questions in every round. Answer for 2 to 4 minutes each.
Any round may hold the technical breadth, the AI/ML depth, or an explain-it-simply question.
One round includes your 8 to 10 minute presentation and Q&A.
Time for your own questions at the end.
unknowns: Which interviewer covers which part of the evaluation is not stated.
Which round holds the presentation is not stated. Be ready to present in any of them.

plan.focus: Stories at full length, and the failure story
plan.gate: All 8 lead stories land between 2:00 and 4:00 with a metric, and the failure worksheet has every box filled.

tasks.text: Read the Amazon answer rubric, then say the 60-second pitch twice.
Say each of the 8 lead stories aloud with the 2 to 4 minute timer. Tick the self-assessment after each one.
Draft the failure story in the worksheet. Every prompt, from a real event.
Say the opening sentence for each of the recruiter's 5 sample questions.
Numbers quiz until every answer is right.

plan.focus: Presentation outline, handout, first timed run
plan.gate: One full run lands between 8:00 and 10:00 with all five sections and a clear call to action.

tasks.text: Read the script cues, then rewrite each section's cues in your own words.
First timed run with the 10-minute timer, out loud and standing. Self-score the six criteria.
Print the one-page handout and check it fits one page. Print 5 copies.
Answer the 15 audience questions aloud, 30 seconds each.
LP bank: two questions for each of the 8 named LPs, with the recommended story.
Second timed run. Fix the section that ran longest.

plan.gate: For any AI/ML question, you give the plain answer first, then the technical one, then survive two follow-ups.

tasks.text: AI/ML cheat sheet: explain every term in one sentence, out loud.
AI/ML basic and intermediate questions: plain answer first, then technical. Mark each Known or Review.
AI/ML deep questions and their probes. Practise saying "I have not worked with that, here is how I would reason about it."
Presentation run 3. Focus on the hook and the call to action.
LP bank: five more questions, timed.

plan.gate: You can explain "what happens when you type a URL" end to end, and pick a database for a scenario with a reason.

tasks.text: Networking cheat sheet and questions. Say "what happens when you type a URL" end to end.
Databases and analytics cheat sheet and questions. Tie in the NetSuite index story.
Security cheat sheet and questions. Explain encryption and IAM to a non-technical customer.
Presentation run 4.
LP bank: five more questions, timed.

plan.focus: CS fundamentals, coding concepts, app development, hardware
plan.gate: You can talk through any of the 10 code drills: what it does, its cost, the bug, the fix.

tasks.text: CS fundamentals questions, out loud: Big-O, data structures, concurrency, memory.
The 10 "walk me through this code" drills, spoken, no typing.
Application development: deployments, observability, queues. Tie in the Oracle numbers.
Hardware basics and the cloud computing pass.
Presentation run 5.

plan.gate: Four mock rounds done and scored; the weakest answer rewritten once. Bag packed by evening.

tasks.text: Mock day: four rounds back to back with a lunch break, as on the real day.
Two more presentation runs. Stop editing the talk after these.
Print the final review, 5 resumes, and 5 handouts. Pack the bag from the day-of list.
Stop by early evening. Sleep is part of the preparation.

plan.gate: Arrive by 9:00 am, calm and fed.

tasks.text: Read the day-of sheet once. Nothing new today.
Say the pitch and the presentation hook once, out loud.
Leave early enough to arrive by 9:00 am.

day_of.arrive: Arrive by 9:00 am. The first interview starts at 9:30 am.

bring.text: Printed final review sheet, for lunch only

notes: No laptop is needed for the presentation. No slides.
Keep the presentation free of any employer's proprietary information.
Lunch is 11:30 am to 12:30 pm. Eat, walk, reread the day-of sheet once. Do not cram.
Track which stories you told in each round so later rounds hear fresh ones.

logistics: Plan the route to campus the night before, with enough buffer to arrive by 9:00 am.
Dress one step above business casual unless told otherwise.
Put your phone on silent before check-in.
